To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of spatiotempornal spreading allows full symbol rate communication over frequency selective channels, and that the use of spatial spreading codes with a suitable diversity scheme (delay diversity) allows full spatial and full spatiotempororal diversity to be exploited.

(1) spatial spreading and delay-diversity are a convenient way to distribute multiple symbol streams over the channel, (2) the approach allows full symbol-rate transmission and full spatiotempral diversity, (3) the approach allows the use of linear codes and hence low complexity, (4) the codes are optimized for maximum coding gain and (5) the approach can be combined with the use of linear space-time codes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1) the derivation of the optimal spatial spreading codes for a MIMO channel with delay spread; 2) a study of the performance of the proposed scheme in terms of coding gain and complexity, as well as the impact of the channel model; and 3) the design of suboptimal receivers for the proposed scheme.
the development of a new class of space-time codes that can be applied to MIMO channels with delay spread.
the design of linear space-time block codes with good performance for channels with delay dispersion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach allows full symbol-rate MIMO transmission with full spatiotempral diversity, hence full capacity, and with a reasonable complexity.
the use of spatial spreading and delay spreading for multiple antenna channels is an interesting alternative to the use of linear space-time codes.
the approach is a very attractive one for the future wireless communication system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spatial spreading is a very promising approach to achieve full diversity and full rate in MIMO systems with delay spread.
we show that spatial spreading codes can achieve full diversity, full rate transmission and full capacity for channels with delay and frequency spread.
we show how spatial spreading and delay spreading can be combined in order to achieve full spatial and delay diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed scheme can achieve the full capacity of the MIMO channel in the presence of frequency selectivity.
spatial spreading codes are a very convenient way to reach full capacity with full diversity.
the spatial spreading approach is a very powerful tool for MIMO systems, and it can be applied to many different scenarios.
